walkthroughs.body_html:
The play is a polemic against capitalism — built for the 1945 election that brought in the Welfare State.

Every Birling stands for an idea. The dining room is a microcosm of Britain.

The play uses a cyclical structure: a second inspector is on his way. Time loops back.

Priestley warns that without genuine change, history repeats — and the older Birlings have learned nothing.

Sheila and Mrs Birling sit on either side of a patriarchy.

Sheila finds her voice; Mrs Birling protects the system that traps her. Top essays unpack this generational and gender divide.
